glosses: The act of fulfilling or the state or quality of being fulfilled; consummation; completion; realization.

examples.text: To achieve fulfilment of one's hopes.
Fulfilment of contractual obligations.
We have yet to see the fulfilment of his potential.
Civilisation has imbued man's minds with false ideas of the evil of sex and its fulfilment.

glosses: A feeling of satisfaction obtained from one's aspirations or needs being fulfilled.

examples.text: What brings you fulfilment in life?
Personal fulfilment comes from having a sense of purpose.

glosses: The activities performed once an order is received to fulfill the order; packaging, distributing and shipping goods.
The process of moving an idea from concept to reality. In business, engineering and other fields, implementation refers to the building process rather than the design process.

examples.text: Now that the requirements are complete we can move on to implementation.

The Group has recently concentrated on two main objectives, the implementation of a Code of Practice on minor station improvements and the preparation of a stock list of approved items of equipment for railway stations.

glosses: A result of implementing something; a finished product, system or device.

examples.text: His implementation works, but it needs some fine-tuning.

glosses: present participle and gerund of carry out

examples.text: In his submission to the UN, [Christof] Heyns points to the experience of drones. glosses: The act of accomplishing; completion; fulfilment.

examples.text: the accomplishment of an enterprise, of a prophecy, etc

glosses: That which completes, perfects, or equips thoroughly; acquirement; attainment; that which constitutes excellence of mind, or elegance of manners, acquired by education or training.

examples.text: I’ll make a proof how I advance in / My new accomplishment of dancing.
Accomplishments have taken virtue’s place, / And wisdom falls before exterior grace ;

glosses: Something accomplished; an achievement.

examples.text: Increasing sales by 20% in the last quarter was seen as a major accomplishment for the business.

glosses: The lexical aspect (aktionsart) of verbs or predicates that change over time until a natural end point.

examples.text: Thus it is attested that some children have taken an accomplishment verb like disappear, which does not have a causative counterpart, and used it as a causative accomplishment in sentences like He disappeared it, i.e. ‘He made it disappear.’

glosses: The act of realizing, as:
An act of figuring out or becoming aware.

examples.text: He came to the startling realization that he had never really known the truth.
A bath is a lovely relaxing event, until the realization that you're soaking in your own crud.

glosses: The act of realizing, as:
The act of making real.

examples.text: The realization of the plan took several years.
He did not stay around long enough to see the realization of the idea.

glosses: The act of realizing, as:
The result of an artistic effort.

examples.text: The painter's realization of her concept was breathtaking.

glosses: The act of realizing, as:
The manner in which a phoneme is pronounced.

examples.text: The realization of -nd as -nn- is not uncommon in the Nuorese dialects.

glosses: The act, manner or style of executing (actions, maneuvers, performances).

examples.text: Already the poor man saw himself crowned by the might of his arm Emperor of Trebizond at least; and so, led away by the intense enjoyment he found in these pleasant fancies, he set himself forthwith to put his scheme into execution.

glosses: The state of being accomplished.

examples.text: The mission's successful execution lifted the troops' morale.

glosses: The act of putting to death or being put to death as a penalty, or actions so associated.
The carrying into effect of a court judgment, or of a will.
Specifically, the seizure of a debtor's goods or property in default of payment.

examples.text: There are two executions in the house, one for sixteen hundred, the other for two thousand three hundred pounds.

glosses: The formal process by which a contract is made valid and put into binding effect.
The carrying out of an instruction, program or program segment by a computer.

examples.text: The entire machine slowed down during the execution of the virus checker.

glosses: Acción o resultado de cumplir.

examples.text: „Das vorangegangene Beispiel zeigt, wie sehr manche daran glauben in einem anderen Menschen oder einer Beziehung die Erfüllung finden zu können.“
